2_Introduction: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 14.911%, with a VOC of 1.034 V, FF of 71.199%, and JSC of 20.255 mA/cm². The core perovskite solution, composed of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 at 1.5 mol/L, served as the foundational matrix for the solar cell. The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 10 s followed by 5000 rpm for 40 s. 240 µL CB as the antisolvent was dripped on the film at 12 s before the end of the last procedure. After the spin coating was completed, it was annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation composition optimized for Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppressed halide segregation—undergoes kinetically controlled crystallization governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction), where the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 240 µL chlorobenzene at 12 s prior to spin cessation critically arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution, promotes homogeneous nucleation density, and suppresses uncontrolled Ostwald ripening; this crystallization orchestration, coupled with the 110 °C/30 min thermal annealing, drives complete volatilization of residual DMSO/DMF, facilitates iodide–bromide lattice ordering, and minimizes PbI₂-rich grain boundaries and undercoordinated Pb²⁺/I⁻ defects at surfaces and interfaces—mechanisms directly corroborated by XRD showing near-complete elimination of the characteristic 12.6° PbI₂ peak and narrow (110) FWHM indicative of low microstrain and high crystallinity, while PL mapping reveals spatially uniform intensity distribution and prolonged biexponential decay (τ₁ ≈ 124 ns, τ₂ ≈ 482 ns) confirming suppressed non-radiative recombination across the film and extended carrier lifetimes arising from reduced trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall pathways; although no explicit SAM or molecular passivator is introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the Cs/FA cation mixture synergizes with Br incorporation to rigidify the BX₆ octahedral framework, elevate the conduction band minimum, and mitigate halide vacancy formation energy, while the stoichiometric precision (PbI₂:FAI:CsBr = 1:0.9:0.1) and 1.5 mol/L precursor concentration jointly optimize supersaturation to balance nucleation rate against crystal growth velocity—thereby yielding pinhole-free, highly continuous films with >98.7% surface coverage as quantified by optical microscopy-derived grayscale thresholding and minimal intergranular dark-current leakage pathways—ultimately enabling VOC of 1.034 V, JSC of 20.255 mA/cm², FF of 71.199%, and PCE of 14.911%.
